methodology.Revenue: The 5% of swap fees burned as RUNE (value to all RUNE holders) plus protocol-kept income (outbound fees net of the gas reimbursed to nodes, slashing fees, developer fund and marketing fund). The node-bonder share of swap fees is treated as a security cost and the LP, affiliate and TCY shares as supplier payments, so none of those count as revenue.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Value paid to suppliers: the node-operator (RUNE bonder) share of swap fees set by the Incentive Pendulum (a security cost), the liquidity-provider share of swap fees (LP side of the Incentive Pendulum), affiliate fees passed through to integrators, the 10% of swap fees paid to TCY stakers, and the outbound gas costs reimbursed from the Reserve to nodes.

methodology.Revenue: 10% protocol fee on both pools. Filecoin: per docs.glif.io/en/for-liquidity-providers/glif-reward-mechanism-ifil iFIL holders earn 90% of SP borrow interest and the protocol treasury takes the remaining 10%, observable on events.glif.link/pool/0/fees. methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 10% protocol fee on both pools. Filecoin: 10% of SP borrow interest goes to the GLIF protocol treasury (events.glif.link/pool/0/fees). Base: 10% of ICN node rewards goes to the protocol treasury (PoolV2.treasuryFee() == 0.1e18).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP yield realised through iFIL / stICNT share-rate appreciation. On Base PoolV2.restakePercentage() == 100% so the LP portion of each reward claim is restaked into the pool and lands on totalAssets() for the next convertToAssets query.

methodology.Fees: Net gaming revenue (NGR) settled to the bankroll, measured as WINR received via ProfitReceived minus WINR paid out via LossCovered. This is an NGR figure standing in for a Fees field that conventionally carries GGR: gross wagered turnover is not observable on-chain because games run off-chain, and creator rewards, affiliate commissions and VIP cashback are already deducted in the off-chain escrow ledger before settlement. NGR is the most complete figure derivable from chain data, and this is a known limitation rather than an omission.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Equal to Fees. All settled net gaming revenue accrues to bankroll liquidity providers through share price appreciation; there is no separate distribution transaction.
methodology.Revenue: Zero. No protocol share is deducted on-chain - a 30 day reconciliation shows 100% of settled net gaming revenue accruing to bankroll liquidity providers through share price appreciation, with no leakage to any other on-chain party. The protocol does capture revenue at the application layer, but it is charged and accounted entirely off-chain and is not derivable from chain data, so it is deliberately not estimated here.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero, for the same reason as Revenue: no protocol share is taken on-chain, and application-layer revenue is not observable from chain data.

Fees.Net Gaming Revenue: WINR received by the bankroll via ProfitReceived minus WINR paid out via LossCovered, per ~5 minute settlement.

SupplySideRevenue.Net Gaming Revenue To LPs: The same net amount, accruing to bankroll liquidity providers through share price appreciation rather than a distribution transaction.

Fees.Trigger Bot Fees: Execution fees paid to keeper bots for limit orders, stop-losses, take-profits, and liquidations.
Fees.Liquidation Fees: When losses reach 85% of collateral (liquidationThresholdF), the position is liquidated and the remaining ~15% of collateral is taken as a fee.
Fees.Funding Fees: LP/reserve portion of funding rate payments. The heavier OI side pays funding; a portion is diverted to the liquidity pool and reserve fund as risk compensation.

methodology.Fees: Every fee charged on a DeepBook trade, paid by both the taker and the maker. The headline rate is 0.1% on volatile pairs and 0.01% on stable pairs, but three pools (DEEP/SUI, DEEP/USDC, wUSDC/USDC) are fee-free and traders who stake enough DEEP pay half the taker fee, so the rate actually collected is lower.
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees left after maker rebates and referral payouts. DeepBook has no way to move collected fees to a treasury, so this money is either burned as DEEP or stays locked in the pool vaults permanently.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero. DeepBook's contracts have no function to move collected trading fees out of a pool, so none of them reach a treasury. The only fee that does is the 500 DEEP charged to create a pool, which is too small to count.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: DEEP burned out of collected trading fees, which permanently shrinks the token supply. Burns are settled in batches, so the amount burned on a given day does not match that day's fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The share of trading fees handed back out: rebates claimed by market makers who stake DEEP, plus fees routed to referrers. Rebates are counted when a maker claims them, which can be days after the trades that earned them. Before April 2025 DeepBook reported claims in a form that gave no reliable date, so supply side revenue is understated for that period and revenue is correspondingly overstated.

Fees.Maker & Taker Fees: Taker and maker fees from every fill on DeepBook's order books.

Revenue.Trading Fees Burned Or Locked In Pool Va: Trading fees left once maker rebates and referral payouts are taken out. This money is either burned as DEEP or stays in the pool vaults.

HoldersRevenue.DEEP Tokens Burned: DEEP burned out of collected trading fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Rebates To Makers: Rebates claimed by market makers who stake DEEP.

methodology.Volume: Total amount staked on bets matched each day. Every bet is funded by two people whose stakes are pooled into a single payout, so both stakes are counted — they are separate money, not the same money counted twice.
methodology.Fees: SX Bet takes no commission on single bets. On parlays it takes 5% of the winner's profit, charged to whichever side wins — market makers pay it too when they win, and losing bets pay nothing. The exchange charged no commission at all between 29 February 2024 and 1 October 2025, and used an earlier fee schedule before that; both are reflected here as reported by the exchange.
methodology.Revenue: Equal to fees, because none of the commission is shared with anyone else.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Zero. Market makers get no share of the commission — they profit from the bets they win. The USDC maker rewards programme is a separate incentive budget, not a cut of fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Through 2025 the collected commission was spent buying SX tokens on the open market.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: From January 2026 the collected commission is sent to the team's treasury instead of funding token buybacks.
methodology.OpenInterest: Total amount staked on bets that have been matched but not yet settled. The exchange only publishes this as a current figure, so it reflects the latest snapshot rather than the state on a past date.

methodology.Revenue: Each pool sets how much of its swap fee the protocol keeps, and HyperSwap switches that on one pool at a time, so the share is read from each pool individually for the day being measured. Pools trade with it switched off until HyperSwap enables it, and those give their entire swap fee to liquidity providers. Every pool that has it enabled currently keeps one sixth. Of whatever the protocol keeps, 25% goes to the treasury and 75% buys back and burns SWAP.

methodology.Fees: The fee taken when a user moves funds out of a shielded pool - a withdrawal, a swap or a bridge transfer - read as the exact amount the pool paid Privacy Cash rather than a modelled rate. methodology.Fees: 3% of each round's total pot, counting both the winning and the losing stakes, taken when the round settles. When a round ends with nobody to pay out - the price finishes exactly where it started, or every bet was on the losing side — the whole pot goes to the treasury instead.

methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue represents the share of swap fees diverted to the protocol. This share is set on a per-pool basis and can be updated by governance. Default share is 0%.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Calculated per-pool. feeProtocol is a uint8 containing two uint4 values: feeProtocol0 (lower 4 bits) and feeProtocol1 (upper 4 bits). If feeProtocol0 = x1 and feeProtocol1 = x2, protocol revenue = Total Fees * (1/x1 + 1/x2) / 2. If only one is set, protocol revenue = Total Fees * 1/x.

methodology.Volume: Volume is the sum of tokenOut amounts from SwapExecuted events emitted by the DEXR FeeAggregatorMaster contract on each supported chain (Base, Optimism, MegaETH, BNB Chain, HyperEVM). tokenOut represents the asset received by the user after the swap completes. methodology.Fees: 3F charges two fees on its leveraged RWA positions. The performance fee is taken on the return of the leveraged collateral, after subtracting the cost of the borrowed debt. The management fee is taken on the full value of the RWA collateral, including the leveraged portion, rather than only the user's deposited capital. Fees are accrued and collected when positions are updated, so a single day can include fees that built up over the preceding days or weeks.
methodology.Revenue: Both the management and performance fees are paid to the protocol, so revenue equals the total fees collected.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Both the management and performance fees are paid to the protocol, so protocol revenue equals the total fees collected.

methodology.Fees: Gross user-paid spend on render jobs under the Burn-Mint Equilibrium model (RNP-001). Each job is priced in USD; an equivalent USD value of RENDER is burned on the Solana SPL mint by the burn wallet. The on-chain burn represents the 95% node-operator side of gross job spend; gross fees are derived by dividing the burn value by 0.95. The remaining 5% Network Operator service fee is paid to OTOY off-chain per the Foundation's documented fee schedule and is not directly observed in the on-chain burn stream. Legacy Ethereum RNDR (pre-2023-11-02 Solana migration) is out of scope.

methodology.Fees: USDC payments received for Mycelia oracle API calls. Each Mycelia API request requires a per-call USDC payment on Base. Transfers where the sender is one of the two Mycelia-controlled wallets are excluded (self-sends and cross-wallet internal transfers).

Fees.Orbis marketplace payouts (80% net): USDC received from the Orbis x402 marketplace facilitator at the configured payout address 0xfF51E0339A17f5fcBa6eAf0E06518d0042ac84bf. Represents 80% of customer payments routed through Orbis (the remaining 20% is retained by Orbis as a facilitator fee). Payouts are batched weekly.

Revenue.Direct settlement: USDC received via the Mycelia-operated TypeScript x402 proxy (myceliasignal-x402-proxy.service), settling directly to 0xD593832Ce9C2B13B192ba50B55dd9AF44e96700d. Represents full gross fees for direct path traffic.

methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees that accrue to holders: the launch LP fee leg spent buying back and burning $HOOK, and the stock pool tax routed to the vault that buys tokenized stocks for holders.

Fees.Bonding Curve Fees: Protocol fee on bonding-curve buys and sells.
Fees.Token Launch Fees: Fees charged to launch a token, across every launch route: the bonding-curve factory, the HookOS-V3 direct-to-DEX launcher and Robinhood Quick Launch. USD-pegged on-chain, so the exact amount paid is used.
Fees.Arena Battle Fees: Protocol cut of settled arena battle pots.
Fees.Graduated V4 Pool Fees: HookOS cut of swaps on graduated Uniswap-v4 pools, taken by HookOSV4Hook and by UniversalGraduationHook.
Fees.Quick Launch Fees: HookOS cut of swaps on Robinhood Quick Launch direct-to-v4 pools, taken by LaunchHook.
Fees.LP Fees: LP fees on the positions HookOS custodies: HookOS-V3 direct-to-DEX launch positions (both the quote leg — native, or the pair token on a non-native-paired launch — and the launched-token leg), graduated Uniswap-v4 positions held by LPFeeSplitter, and locked positions held by LPLocker.
Fees.HOOK Pool Tax: Tax skimmed from the WETH leg of every $HOOK Uniswap-v4 swap.
Fees.Service Fees: Wallet Pro subscription fees.
Fees.Presale Fees: Percentage of the raise taken when a presale settles, plus the flat presale creation fee.
Fees.Trading Fees: Skim on buys and sells routed through the HookOS trading bot.
Fees.Stock Pool Tax: Tax on tokenized-stock pool swaps, taken on the pool's quote leg (read live from the hook — WETH on the current Robinhood deployment).
Fees.Tournament Fees: Protocol cut of tournament and event prize pools.
Fees.Protocol Fees: Native fees routed to FeeRouter by a HookOS module not individually mapped.
Fees.Creator Fees: Share of trading and LP fees routed to token creators.
Fees.Hook Author Fees: Share of the protocol fee credited to the authors of the hooks a token runs.

HoldersRevenue.Vault Fees to Burn: 95% of the vault fees are used to buy PEA and burned.

Buy-side pool fees are charged on the USDT0 input (exact); sell-side pool fees are charged in the traded token and valued as their USDT0 equivalent at that swap's own price (usdtOut/99).
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the 1% trade fee; there is no token-creation fee.
methodology.Revenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the Prismapad treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the Prismapad treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the launched token's creator (v1: claimable from the launchpad; v2/v3: collected from the locked pool position).

Fees.Token Swap Fees: 1% fee on every trade: bonding-curve trades (v1) and swaps in launchpad-created StableSwap pools (v2/v3).

Revenue.Trade fees to protocol: The protocol's 50% share of the 1% trade fee.

ProtocolRevenue.Trade fees to protocol: The protocol's 50% share of the 1% trade fee.

SupplySideRevenue.Trade fees to token creators: The token creator's 50% share of the 1% trade fee.

methodology.Volume: Total ETH wagered across all lottery rounds, derived from staker rewards (a flat 6% of each round's pot).
methodology.Fees: The 10% rake taken from every round's pot: 6% to veSTEEL stakers, 2% to the keeper, and 2% to the motherlode.
methodology.Revenue: Gross profit: 6% distributed to veSTEEL stakers plus the 2% keeper cut.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 2% keeper self-funding cut retained by the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veSTEEL stakers (RewardNotified events on VeSteelV2).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% of each pot routed to the motherlode, paid back out to winning players.

Fees.Staking Rewards: 6% of each pot distributed to veSTEEL stakers (RewardNotified events).
Fees.Rake to Keeper: 2% of each pot self-funding the keeper.
Fees.Rake to Motherlode: 2% of each pot routed to the motherlode.

Revenue.Staking Rewards: 6% of each pot distributed to veSTEEL stakers.
Revenue.Rake to Keeper: 2% of each pot self-funding the keeper.

ProtocolRevenue.Rake to Keeper: 2% of each pot retained by the protocol for keeper operations.

HoldersRevenue.Staking Rewards: 6% of each pot distributed to veSTEEL stakers.

SupplySideRevenue.Rake to Motherlode: 2% of each pot routed to the motherlode, paid back out to winning players.

methodology.Volume: Gross ETH paid by purchasers for acquisitions (pulls), net of refunded, expired, or slippage-cancelled requests.
methodology.Fees: Net Acquisition fees paid by NFT purchasers, plus settlement fees taken from listing backings.
methodology.Revenue: Team share of the protocol's cut of acquisition and settlement fees, plus any fees diverted to FWA-token buybacks.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Team share of the protocol's fee cut, per the Splitter contract's live split.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: FWA-token buybacks funded from protocol fees, plus retroactive scheduled buybacks funded from previously earned team fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of net acquisition fees distributed to NFT depositors (equal split across active listings plus the top-listing pot), plus the snapshot soulbound-NFT holders' share of protocol fees via the Splitter.

Fees.Acquisition Fees: The total ETH paid by purchasers to acquire a random NFT from the pool, net of refunded requests and of quick-sell payouts returned to purchasers (85% of the listing backing when they accept the depositor's standing bid).
Fees.Settlement Fees: 1% of the listing backing, charged when a settlement returns the backing to the depositor (purchaser keeps or relists the NFT).
Fees.Retained Settlement Penalties: 15% of the listing backing retained when a purchaser accepts the depositor's standing bid instead of keeping the NFT.

Revenue.Settlement Fees: Settlement fees accrue entirely to the protocol.
Revenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained settlement penalties accrue to the protocol.
Revenue.Token Buy Back: Protocol fees diverted to FWA-token buybacks.

SupplySideRevenue.Acquisition Fees: Share of net acquisition fees distributed to NFT depositors, split equally across active listings.
SupplySideRevenue.Top Listing Reward: Share of acquisition fees accruing to the depositor of the top-backed listing.
SupplySideRevenue.Acquisition Fees to Snapshot NFT Holders: Snapshot soulbound-NFT holders' share (via the Splitter) of the protocol's cut of acquisition fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Settlement Fees to Snapshot NFT Holders: Snapshot soulbound-NFT holders' share (via the Splitter) of settlement fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Retained Settlement Penalties to Snapsho: Snapshot soulbound-NFT holders' share (via the Splitter) of retained settlement penalties.
SupplySideRevenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Settlement discount redistributed among active NFT depositors.

ProtocolRevenue.Settlement Fees: Settlement fees accrue entirely to the protocol.
ProtocolRevenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained settlement penalties accrue to the protocol.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: Protocol fees diverted to FWA-token buybacks.
HoldersRevenue.Retroactive buybacks: Scheduled FWA-token buybacks (327 ETH in 1 ETH slices every 2 hours) funded from previously earned team fees.

methodology.Revenue: The 10% performance fee taken from collected trading fees and sent to the protocol treasury (fees / fee, with the divisor read from each ZeroBurn event).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — the 10% performance fee retained by the protocol treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 90% of collected trading fees that are compounded back to LPs.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: All Uniswap V3 trading fees collected by the positions each Tirelire Hypervisor manages, summed on-chain from ZeroBurn events.

Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The 10% performance fee taken from collected trading fees and sent to the protocol treasury (fees / fee, with the divisor read from each ZeroBurn event).

ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The 10% performance fee taken from collected trading fees and sent to the protocol treasury (fees / fee, with the divisor read from each ZeroBurn event).

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to LPs: The 90% of collected trading fees that are compounded back to LPs.

methodology.Fees: Includes swap fees and bribes paid by protocols
methodology.Revenue: Revenue going to the protocol + Token holder Revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Swap fees going to the protocol
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees distributed to holders and all the bribes go to holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees distributed to LPs (from gauged pools).

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Fees paid by users on each swap.

Revenue.Bribes to holders: Bribes paid by protocols to holders

HoldersRevenue.Bribes to holders: Bribes paid by protocols to holders
HoldersRevenue.Sarcophagus fee reclassification: Reclassifies fees already accrued as protocol revenue into holder revenue when funded to Sarcophagus.

methodology.Fees: Quote-denominated swap fees plus token-launch fees paid through o1 Launchpad. Legacy swap fees paid in launched tokens are excluded because they cannot be priced consistently.
methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders plus token-launch fees paid by creators.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform share of swap fees plus token-launch fees received by the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees allocated to token creators and referrers.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: No fees are distributed to token holders.

Fees.Token Launch Fees: Fees charged when a token is launched through a current production factory.

UserFees.Token Launch Fees: Fees paid by creators when launching a token.

Revenue.Token Launch Fees to Protocol: Token-launch fees received by the platform treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Token Launch Fees to Protocol: Token-launch fees received by the platform treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees to Referrers: Swap fees allocated to valid referrers.

methodology.Fees: Odinbot charges a 1% fee on copy-trades (min 0.001 SOL for spot copy trades and 0.1% of position size for perpetual copy trades). Total fees are the protocol share received by the Odin fee wallet plus affiliate payouts in the same transaction.
methodology.UserFees: Odinbot charges a 1% fee on copy-trades (min 0.001 SOL for spot copy trades and 0.1% of position size for perpetual copy trades). Total fees are the protocol share received by the Odin fee wallet plus affiliate payouts in the same transaction.
methodology.Revenue: The 60% (100% if no referral code is applied) protocol share of Odinbot trading fees retained after affiliate payouts.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 60% (100% if no referral code is applied) protocol share of Odinbot trading fees retained after affiliate payouts.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 40% affiliate commission paid to referrers in the same transaction, if a referral code is applied.

Fees.Trading Fees: 1% of trade value, min 0.001 SOL for spot copy trades and 0.1% of position size for perpetual copy trades, including affiliate payouts.

UserFees.Trading Fees: 1% of trade value, min 0.001 SOL for spot copy trades and 0.1% of position size for perpetual copy trades, including affiliate payouts.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees: 60% (100% if no referral code is applied) protocol share of Odinbot trading fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Referral Fees: 40% affiliate commission paid to referrers in the same transaction, if a referral code is applied.

methodology.Volume: Sum of the input amount of every executed order, taken from the router's OrderExecuted logs. Only the input leg is counted, so a single trade is never counted twice. Cancellations, which the previous router encoded as an OrderExecuted with orderType 255, are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Protocol fee deducted from the output token of each executed order. The rate is signed by the maker as part of the order and capped on-chain at 1%.
methodology.Revenue: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None. Liquidity is Uniswap's; its pool fees are not counted here.

Fees.Protocol Fees: Protocol fee deducted from the output token of each executed order. The rate is signed by the maker as part of the order payload and capped on-chain at 1%.

Revenue.Protocol Fees: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.

methodology.Fees: USDG token-creation fees plus all trading fees from BowYard's classic and Agent bonding curves and post-graduation DEX pools.
methodology.UserFees: All creation and trading fees paid by BowYard users, denominated in USDG.
methodology.Revenue: Fees paid to the BowYard protocol treasury: the full classic token-creation fee, the classic protocol share of curve/DEX fees, and the immutable 20% protocol share of Agent trading fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The full classic token-creation fee, the classic protocol share of curve/DEX fees, and 20% of Agent trading fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Classic creator fee shares plus the Agent market shares routed to creators, operating recipients, and attributed ecosystem recipients.

Fees.Token Creation Fees: The fixed USDG fee charged when a classic BowYard token is created.
Fees.Bonding Curve Trading Fees: Protocol and creator fees charged on classic bonding-curve trades.
Fees.BowYard DEX Swap Fees: Protocol and creator fees charged by BowYard's permanently locked classic DEX pools.
Fees.Agent Bonding Curve Trading Fees: The aggregate 1% fee charged on Agent bonding-curve trades.
Fees.Agent DEX Swap Fees: The aggregate 1% fee charged by graduated Agent DEX pools.

Revenue.Token Creation Fees to Protocol: The full classic token-creation fee paid to the protocol treasury.
Revenue.Bonding Curve Fees to Protocol: The protocol share of classic bonding-curve fees.
Revenue.BowYard DEX Fees to Protocol: The protocol share of classic BowYard DEX fees.
Revenue.Agent Trading Fees to Protocol: The immutable 20% protocol share of Agent trading fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Token Creation Fees to Protocol: The full classic token-creation fee paid to the protocol treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Bonding Curve Fees to Protocol: The protocol share of classic bonding-curve fees.
ProtocolRevenue.BowYard DEX Fees to Protocol: The protocol share of classic BowYard DEX fees.
ProtocolRevenue.Agent Trading Fees to Protocol: The immutable 20% protocol share of Agent trading fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Bonding Curve Fees to Creators: The creator share of classic bonding-curve fees.
SupplySideRevenue.BowYard DEX Fees to Creators: The creator share of classic BowYard DEX fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Agent Trading Fees to Creators: The immutable 20% creator share of Agent trading fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Agent Trading Fees to Operators and Ecos: The remaining 60% of Agent trading fees routed to the operating recipient and, when attributed, the ecosystem recipient.

methodology.Fees: 1% swap fees from bow.fun factory-launched Uniswap V3 pools on Robinhood Chain, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.Revenue: 65% of swap fees retained by the bow.fun protocol, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 65% of swap fees retained by the bow.fun protocol, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 35% of swap fees routed to launched-token creators, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: 1% swap fees from bow.fun factory-launched Uniswap V3 pools.

Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol's 65% share of swap fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol's 65% share of swap fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: The launched token creator's 35% share of swap fees.

methodology.Fees: Total swap fees, priced in the valued leg's token. Per-swap fee = amount x (pool.fee / 1e6) where pool.fee is the value live at the swap's block_time (sourced from init_dex plus every update_fee_and_revenue_cut call, window-joined via effective range). Exact-in swaps are valued on the input leg (amount_in call argument), exact-out swaps on the output leg (amount_out call argument). Per-pool token identity comes from the swap calls, with dex_call_init_dex as a fallback for pools that have never traded.
methodology.Revenue: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP share of swap fees plus Fluid's protocol share. LP share = fees x (1 - revenue_cut/1e6). Fluid receives 50% of the protocol cut per Jupiter Lend / Fluid arrangement.

Fees.Jupiter Lend Dex Swap Fees: Total swap fees, priced in the valued leg's token.

Revenue.Jupiter Lend Dex Swap Fees to Protocol: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.

ProtocolRevenue.Jupiter Lend Dex Swap Fees to Protocol: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.

SupplySideRevenue.Jupiter Lend Dex Swap Fees to LPs: LP share of swap fees. LP share = fees x (1 - revenue_cut/1e6).
SupplySideRevenue.Jupiter Lend Dex Swap Fees to Fluid: Fluid's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.

methodology.Fees: Total fees paid by users on AGNT: (1) the 1.095% Doppler V4 terminal pool fee on tokens launched via the launchpad on Base + Robinhood Chain, derived from the observed on-chain platform fee share (WETH on Base; WETH plus RWA numeraires — tokenized stocks like AAPL that a Robinhood launch pairs against, e.g. $BEER — on Robinhood, priced by DefiLlama; the unpriced launched-token leg is excluded, a conservative lower bound); plus (2) the 0.40% platform fee on in-app swaps (Base), measured as WETH + USDC paid by Relay to AGNT's app-fee recipient wallet; plus (3) fees from PonsV2 launches on Robinhood Chain, read from each token's AgntFeeWedge Split events (native-ETH leg = total user-paid fee).
methodology.Revenue: Fees kept by AGNT: the 32% platform share of launchpad pool fees (WETH released by the Doppler initializers on Base + Robinhood, to 0x5bF5805e…C5f0) plus 100% of the 0.40% swap fee (WETH + USDC paid by Relay on Base to the app-fee recipient wallets — 0x585b6854…0598 pre-repoint and 0x5bF5805e…C5f0 post-repoint) plus AGNT's ~2/7 (28.57%) protocol cut of PonsV2 launch fees on Robinhood (the `toAgnt` leg of each AgntFeeWedge Split; the remaining 5/7 is forwarded to each token's own engine).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — all AGNT launchpad fees accrue to the platform treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 68% of launchpad pool fees paid to third-party token creators (63%) and the Doppler protocol (~5%), estimated from the observed platform WETH share.

Fees.Launchpad Fees: 1.095% Doppler terminal fee (WETH leg), estimated as platform WETH share / 0.32, on Base + Robinhood Chain.
Fees.Trading Fees: 0.40% swap fee (Base), WETH + USDC paid by Relay to the app-fee recipient wallet.
Fees.Pons Launchpad Fees: PonsV2 launch fees on Robinhood Chain (native-ETH leg), the `total` of each token's AgntFeeWedge Split event.

Revenue.Launchpad Fees to Protocol: 32% platform share, WETH released to the fee wallet on Base + Robinhood
Revenue.Trading Fees to Protocol: 100% of the 0.40% swap fee, WETH + USDC paid by Relay to the app-fee recipient (Base)
Revenue.Pons Fees to Protocol: AGNT's ~2/7 (28.57%) cut of PonsV2 launch fees, the `toAgnt` leg of each AgntFeeWedge Split (Robinhood).

ProtocolRevenue.Launchpad Fees to Protocol: 32% platform share, WETH released to the fee wallet on Base + Robinhood
ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees to Protocol: 100% of the 0.40% swap fee, WETH + USDC paid by Relay to the app-fee recipient (Base)
ProtocolRevenue.Pons Fees to Protocol: AGNT's ~2/7 (28.57%) cut of PonsV2 launch fees, the `toAgnt` leg of each AgntFeeWedge Split (Robinhood).

SupplySideRevenue.Launchpad Fees to Creators: 63% of launchpad pool fees paid to third-party token creators
SupplySideRevenue.Launchpad Fees to Doppler: 5% of launchpad pool fees paid to the Doppler protocol
SupplySideRevenue.Pons Fees to Engine: The ~5/7 (71.43%) of each PonsV2 launch fee forwarded from the AgntFeeWedge to the token's own engine (Robinhood).

methodology.Volume: Total ETH wagered across all bets each round, derived from staker rewards (a flat 8% of wagers).
methodology.Fees: The 10% rake taken from every round's wagers: 8% distributed to veNFT stakers plus 2% routed to the vault.
methodology.Revenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veNFT stakers (RewardDistributed events on CashVoteEscrowStaking).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veNFT stakers.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% of wagers routed to the vault pool, which is paid back out to winning players.

Fees.Staking Rewards: 8% of wagers distributed to veNFT stakers (RewardDistributed events).
Fees.Wagers to Jackpot Vault: 2% of wagers routed to the vault pool.

Revenue.Staking Rewards: 8% of wagers distributed to veNFT stakers.

HoldersRevenue.Staking Rewards: 8% of wagers distributed to veNFT stakers.

SupplySideRevenue.Wagers to Jackpot Vault: 2% of wagers routed to the vault pool, paid back out to winning players.

methodology.Volume: Total ETH planted on the grid, taken from the Planted and PlantedMany events.
methodology.Fees: Every plant pays an admin fee, at the configured adminFeeBps rate (1% at time of writing), on the AAPL bought with it. Every revealed round with a winner pays that round's configured rakeBps on the loss pool (the stakes on the 24 plots that did not bloom), split into a fixed 10% to SEED stakers (STAKERS_BPS, a contract constant), the round's configured jackpotBps share to the Golden Apple jackpot, and the remainder to the treasury. Rounds where the blooming plot is empty take no rake — the whole pot rolls into the jackpot.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees — both the admin fee and the rake are paid by players out of what they planted.
methodology.Revenue: Gross profit: the admin fee plus the stakers and treasury cuts of the rake. The jackpot cut is excluded because it is paid back out to players.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The admin fee taken on every plant at the configured adminFeeBps rate, withdrawn by the owner via collectAdmin.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value reaching SEED holders: the fixed 10% of each round's rake flushed to SeedStaking as AAPL yield for stakers, plus the treasury remainder that buys SEED back on the DEX and burns it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The round's configured jackpotBps share of its rake, routed to the Golden Apple jackpot and paid back out to players when it hits.

Fees.Admin Fee: The configured adminFeeBps share of the AAPL bought on every plant (Planted and PlantedMany events), resolved per event so rate changes apply only from the block they take effect.
Fees.RAKE: The rake taken on every revealed round with a winner.

UserFees.Admin Fee: The configured adminFeeBps share of the AAPL bought on every plant (Planted and PlantedMany events), resolved per event so rate changes apply only from the block they take effect.
UserFees.RAKE: The rake taken on every revealed round with a winner.

Revenue.Admin Fee: Admin fee on every plant, at the configured adminFeeBps rate.
Revenue.Rake to Stakers: The fixed 10% staker share of each round's rake.
Revenue.Rake to Buyback: The treasury remainder of each round's rake used to buy SEED back on the DEX and burn it.

ProtocolRevenue.Admin Fee: Admin fee on every plant at the configured adminFeeBps rate, withdrawn by the owner via collectAdmin.

HoldersRevenue.Rake to Stakers: The fixed 10% staker share of each round's rake, flushed to SeedStaking as AAPL yield for SEED stakers.
HoldersRevenue.Rake to Buyback: The treasury remainder of each round's rake, spent buying SEED back on the DEX and burning it.

SupplySideRevenue.Rake to Jackpot: The round's configured jackpotBps share of its rake, routed to the Golden Apple jackpot and paid back out to players when it hits.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% Motherlode jackpot and 1% Eclipse prize pool funded by each mining round, both paid back out to players.

Fees.Protocol Fees: 1% of each mining round pot and 5% of each Eclipse beacon purchase, retained by the protocol.
Fees.Prize Pools: 2% of each mining round pot to the Motherlode jackpot and 1% to the Eclipse prize pool.

Revenue.Staking Rewards: 8% of each mining round pot and 10% of each beacon purchase, distributed to LUNA stakers.
Revenue.Protocol Fees: 1% of each mining round pot and 5% of each beacon purchase, retained by the protocol.

HoldersRevenue.Staking Rewards: 8% of each mining round pot and 10% of each beacon purchase, distributed to LUNA stakers.

SupplySideRevenue.Prize Pools: The 2% Motherlode jackpot and 1% Eclipse prize pool, paid back out to players.

methodology.Volume: Sum of `price * amount` for every TradeRecorded event emitted by Primit's TradeRecorder contract (0xC005A9bb11f162329f3EfCCc35F69F9Bb635EeC6 on Avalanche C-Chain) during the UTC day, excluding self-trades where taker == maker. Both `price` and `amount` are 1e18 fixed-point, so the product is scaled by 1e36 and normalized down to floating USD before returning. Data is 100% reconstructable on-chain — no dependency on any Primit-operated HTTP endpoint. Every fill matched or routed by Primit is captured by this single TradeRecorder event stream, so there is no separate broker-level attribution to deduplicate against.

methodology.Fees: Everything users paid the protocol: all native revenue arriving at the chain's fee collector — the PlatformFeeCollector on Robinhood Chain, a bridging collector on each satellite — from the 2% presale service fee, launch tokens' master fee, the bonding pad's 0.5% per-trade skim, the instant-launch fee and the locker's fee-claim cut (FeesReceived logs), PLUS the 10% referrer share carved off the user-attributed streams before they reach the collector (ReferralPaid logs). Satellite revenue is counted on the chain that earned it and excluded from Robinhood when it arrives bridged, so it counts once.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees the protocol keeps: collector receipts only, so the referrer share is excluded. The protocol retains all of it, with the home-chain split between governance holders and the treasury reported under HoldersRevenue / ProtocolRevenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 10% referrer share, the one part of a fee the protocol does not keep — paid out by the ReferralRegistry to the trader's referrer before the remainder reaches the collector (ReferralPaid logs).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of every home-chain distribution delivered to GovernanceToken holders as native-ETH dividends (FeesDistributed logs; distributions happen only on Robinhood Chain).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of every home-chain distribution delivered to the protocol owner (FeesDistributed logs; distributions happen only on Robinhood Chain).

Fees.Platform Fees: Revenue received by the chain's fee collector (PlatformFeeCollector on Robinhood Chain; a bridging collector on each satellite) from every protocol stream: the 2% presale service fee, launch tokens' master fee, the bonding pad's 0.5% per-trade skim, the instant-launch fee, and the locker's fee-claim cut. From FeesReceived logs. Bridge re-deliveries are excluded on Robinhood so satellite revenue counts once, at origin.
Fees.Fees Paid Out To Referrers: The 10% referrer share carved off the user-attributed streams (pad trade skim, presale service fee, instant-launch fee) by the ReferralRegistry before the remainder reaches the collector — paid by the user, kept by the referrer, so it counts as fees but not as protocol revenue (ReferralPaid logs).

Revenue.Platform Fees Retained By The Protocol: Every fee that reaches the collector is retained by the protocol and later split between governance holders and the treasury on the home chain — see HoldersRevenue / ProtocolRevenue for the split.

SupplySideRevenue.Fees Paid Out To Referrers: The referrer's 10% cut, paid out before the remainder reaches the collector (ReferralPaid logs).

HoldersRevenue.Fees To Governance Holders: The share of every distribution paid to GovernanceToken holders as native-ETH dividends (holdersAmount of FeesDistributed).

ProtocolRevenue.Fees To Treasury: The share of every distribution paid to the protocol owner (ownerAmount of FeesDistributed).

Revenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained settlement backing kept by the protocol.
Revenue.Swap Fees: Hook swap fees accrue entirely to the protocol.

ProtocolRevenue.Acquisition Fees: Protocol cut of acquisition fees paid to the treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Settlement Fees: Settlement fees paid to the treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained settlement penalties paid to the treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees: Hook swap fees paid to the treasury.

HoldersRevenue.RIP Buyback: Protocol fees diverted to RIP buybacks.

SupplySideRevenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained settlement penalties redistributed among active depositors when not routed to the protocol.

methodology.Fees: Uniswap V3 swap fees generated by Goon-launched pools (pools with under $100 TVL are excluded as dust).
methodology.Revenue: The USD share of swap fees, minus whatever Uniswap's protocol fee switch (read live per pool via slot0().feeProtocol) diverts to Uniswap itself.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The token share of swap fees paid to the token creator, plus Uniswap's diverted cut of both swap fee legs (read live per pool via slot0().feeProtocol).

ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Swap fees charged when USD was the input token, minus Uniswap's live per-pool protocol fee cut, accrue to the protocol treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: Swap fees charged when the Token was the input token, minus Uniswap's live per-pool protocol fee cut, accrue to the token creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Uniswap: Uniswap's protocol fee switch cut of both swap fee legs, read live per pool via slot0().feeProtocol - no longer reaches Goon's protocol or the token creator.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All gross gaming revenue is kept by the protocol treasury.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by users. V2 pools charge a fixed 0.3%; V3 pools use their configured fee tier.

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Meme Token Buybacks: Part of (0% when buyback is disabled, 35% when buyback is enabled) the uniswap v4 swap fees collected goes to the buyback and burning of meme tokens

Traders also pay Uniswap's own 0.04% protocol fee on pools where it is switched on; that is Uniswap's charge, not pools.trade's, and is left out here.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The whole 0.25% trading fee: the creator's share plus the part that is compounded back into the locked liquidity.
methodology.Revenue: Zero. pools.trade keeps none of the trading fee — it all goes to the token's creator and back into the pool's own permanently locked liquidity.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero. pools.trade has no treasury cut, no launch fee and no graduation fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero. There is no pools.trade token.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: 0.25% of every trade, read per trade from the swap's own fee rate with Uniswap's separate 0.04% protocol fee removed.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The creator vault's share of fees charged in ETH (i.e. on buys), read from each pool's FeeSplitter.getSplits() — 40% on current deployments. Only paid on launches created with the creator fee enabled, and never out of fees charged in the token.
SupplySideRevenue.Fees Compounded Into Locked Liquidity: Everything else, added straight back into the pool's permanently locked position instead of being paid out to anyone.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fees (CreatorFeeCollected) paid out to each pool's creator.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perps, spot and HIP-4 prediction-market trades executed through Liquary (formerly Hypersight).
methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid by users on trades executed through Liquary (0.05% on perps and on HIP-4 prediction-market closes).
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Liquary from Hyperliquid trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by Liquary from Hyperliquid trades.

ProtocolRevenue.Hyperliquid Builder Code Fees: Builder code fees collected by the builder.

methodology.Volume: Gross ETH notional (fees included) of buys and sells executed on Frontier bonding curves (v1 and v1.2), taken directly from each shared BondingCurve contract's Buy/Sell events, plus the ETH leg of every swap on a Frontier Uniswap V4 pool (graduated curves and v1.2 direct-seed launches alike), read from the canonical PoolManager's Swap events and filtered to the pools registered on Frontier's FactoryHook, excluding wash trading by the same rule as the uniswap-v4 adapter (pools whose daily trades come from too few distinct addresses to be organic, unless the coin is a core asset or CoinGecko-listed). Those V4 swaps are also counted by the uniswap-v4 adapter on Robinhood Chain, which is why this adapter is flagged doublecounted.
methodology.Fees: The bonding-curve trade fee charged on every buy and sell (1.5% of the trade's cost at the time of writing), the fees a token pays out of the ETH it raised when its curve fills and seeds its Uniswap V4 pool, the FactoryHook fee taken on every swap of a Frontier V4 pool (a hook delta on top of the pool's LP fee, so not part of uniswap-v4's fees), and the LP fees of the protocol's permanently locked seed positions, counted on a realized basis when they are collected (Harvester.collect is permissionless, so a collection carries the fees accrued since the previous one and lands on the collection day, not the days they were earned). v1 reconstructs the trade fee from the on-chain txFee timeline and graduation payouts from WETH transfers; v1.2 reads everything exactly from CurveFeeDistributed, GraduationFeesPaid, SwapFeeDistributed and the PolDistributor's FeesDistributed.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders out of their trade or out of the ETH they raised.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue across both deployments: on v1, the protocol's 25% of the bonding-curve trade fee net of referrer rewards plus the factory owner's graduation share; on v1.2, the residual share of the trade fee after referrer and creator cuts (creator share owner-tunable via creatorShareBps), the protocol's graduation share, the protocol owner's share of the hook fee on every V4 swap, and the protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees. Frontier has no protocol token, so there is no holders revenue and Revenue equals ProtocolRevenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: v1: 25% of the curve trade fee net of referrer rewards, plus WETH sent to the factory owner at graduation. v1.2: residual share of the curve trade fee (50% at the time of writing, net of referrer rewards), its share of graduation payouts (0% at the time of writing), the protocol owner's share of the V4 hook fee (protocolFeeRatio, owner-tunable) and the protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: v1: the creator's 75% of every curve trade fee, referrer rewards, and the 5% graduation fee to the token creator. v1.2: the creator's share of every curve trade fee (50% at the time of writing), referrer rewards, the 5% graduation fee to the creator, the graduation refund to the caller (0% at the time of writing), and the after-protocol remainder of the V4 hook fee and of collected seed-position LP fees, split between the coin's staking vault and its fee recipient (the creator).

Fees.Curve Trade Fees: Trade fee withheld by the bonding curve on every buy and sell, at the on-chain txFee rate (150 bps at the time of writing). v1 reconstructs it from Buy/Sell and TxFeeUpdated; v1.2 emits it per trade as CurveFeeDistributed.
Fees.Graduation Fees: Fees paid in WETH out of the ETH a token raised when its curve fills. v1 classifies WETH transfers to the creator (5%) and factory owner (0% at the time of writing); v1.2 uses GraduationFeesPaid (creator 5%, protocol 0%, caller refund 0% at the time of writing). The ETH that seeds the Uniswap V4 pool is liquidity, not a fee, and is excluded.
Fees.Pool Swap Fees: The FactoryHook's fee on every swap of a Frontier Uniswap V4 pool, from SwapFeeDistributed: a volatility-scaled hook delta charged on top of the pool's LP fee, in the swap's input currency (native ETH or the coin). The LP fee itself belongs to uniswap-v4 and is not counted here.
Fees.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Fees: Uniswap V4 LP fees of the protocol's permanently locked seed positions, counted on a realized basis when Harvester.collect forwards them to the PolDistributor (FeesDistributed), in WETH and the coin. A collection carries everything accrued since the previous one, so these land on the collection day rather than the days they were earned. These are also LP fees in uniswap-v4's figures.

UserFees.Curve Trade Fees: Trade fee withheld by the bonding curve on every buy and sell, at the on-chain txFee rate (150 bps at the time of writing). v1 reconstructs it from Buy/Sell and TxFeeUpdated; v1.2 emits it per trade as CurveFeeDistributed.
UserFees.Graduation Fees: Fees paid in WETH out of the ETH a token raised when its curve fills. v1 classifies WETH transfers to the creator (5%) and factory owner (0% at the time of writing); v1.2 uses GraduationFeesPaid (creator 5%, protocol 0%, caller refund 0% at the time of writing). The ETH that seeds the Uniswap V4 pool is liquidity, not a fee, and is excluded.
UserFees.Pool Swap Fees: The FactoryHook's fee on every swap of a Frontier Uniswap V4 pool, from SwapFeeDistributed: a volatility-scaled hook delta charged on top of the pool's LP fee, in the swap's input currency (native ETH or the coin). The LP fee itself belongs to uniswap-v4 and is not counted here.
UserFees.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Fees: Uniswap V4 LP fees of the protocol's permanently locked seed positions, counted on a realized basis when Harvester.collect forwards them to the PolDistributor (FeesDistributed), in WETH and the coin. A collection carries everything accrued since the previous one, so these land on the collection day rather than the days they were earned. These are also LP fees in uniswap-v4's figures.

Revenue.Curve Trade Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of the bonding-curve trade fee, net of the referrer's share on referred trades (25% on v1; residual after creator/referrer on v1.2, 50% at the time of writing).
Revenue.Graduation Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of the graduation payout.
Revenue.Pool Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol owner's share of the V4 hook fee (protocolFeeRatio, owner-tunable), taken off the top on every swap.
Revenue.POL Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Curve Trade Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of the bonding-curve trade fee, net of the referrer's share on referred trades (25% on v1; residual after creator/referrer on v1.2, 50% at the time of writing).
ProtocolRevenue.Graduation Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of the graduation payout.
ProtocolRevenue.Pool Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol owner's share of the V4 hook fee (protocolFeeRatio, owner-tunable), taken off the top on every swap.
ProtocolRevenue.POL Fees to Protocol: The protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Trade Fees to Creators: The token creator's share of every bonding-curve trade fee (75% on v1; owner-tunable, 50% at the time of writing on v1.2).
SupplySideRevenue.Curve Trade Fees to Referrers: The referrer's share of the curve trade fee on a referred trade, paid in WETH.
SupplySideRevenue.Graduation Fees to Creators: The graduation fee paid to the token creator, 5% of the ETH its curve raised.
SupplySideRevenue.Graduation Refund to Caller: The v1.2 graduation refund paid to the caller who triggered graduation (0% at the time of writing).
SupplySideRevenue.Pool Swap Fees to Stakers: The coin's staking vault's share of the V4 hook fee, after the protocol's cut (communityFeeRatio, fixed per pool at launch).
SupplySideRevenue.Pool Swap Fees to Creators: The coin's fee recipient's (creator's) share of the V4 hook fee, after the protocol's cut.
SupplySideRevenue.POL Fees to Stakers: The coin's staking vault's share of collected seed-position LP fees.
SupplySideRevenue.POL Fees to Creators: The coin creator's share of collected seed-position LP fees.

methodology.Fees: The arbitrage profit the hook realises and pays out, summed from the ProfitCurrencyDistribute event the hook emits on every distribution. The hook closes the price gap a swap opens between connected pools within the same transaction, so this is value recaptured from MEV rather than a fee charged to anyone.
methodology.Revenue: Zero. The hook retains none of the profit it captures — every distribution pays out in full to the trader and the pool's LPs in the triggering transaction, and the hook and its arbitrage executors hold no balance.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: All of the captured profit: the rebate paid to the trader whose swap created the opportunity, plus the amount donated to the LPs of the pool it was taken from.
methodology.UserFees: Zero. Users are not charged by the hook; a swapper receives the rebate leg rather than paying anything.

Fees.MEV Rewards: Arbitrage profit captured by the hook when a swap moves one pool away from a connected pool, closed out in the same transaction.

SupplySideRevenue.MEV Rewards To Traders: Rebate paid to the trader whose swap created the arbitrage opportunity.
SupplySideRevenue.MEV Rewards To LPs: Donated to the liquidity providers of the pool the profit was taken from.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged on Hookers launches, in native ETH. A creator picks a launch style from the protocol's mechanism registry. Hooked styles skim a directional buy/sell fee inside the hook, set by the creator between 100 and 1000 bps. Hookless styles use the pool's own Uniswap v4 LP fee, collected through LiquidityCustody. The registry is read on chain, so styles added later are included automatically.
methodology.Revenue: The 30 bps protocol fee routed to FeeRouter, plus the share spent buying back and burning HKRS, the protocol's own token.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: A flat 30 bps of trade volume routed to FeeRouter. It is carved out of the creator's advertised fee rather than added on top, and applies identically to every launch style.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: HKRS bought back and burned, valued in ETH. This covers the automatic buyback hook on the HKRS pool, plus the discretionary buybacks the team runs out of the protocol's fee share, which are measured from the HKRS burned and priced from the HKRS pool. Buybacks on third-party launches are excluded and counted as supply side, since they accrue to those tokens' holders. Discretionary buybacks are funded from fees already counted as protocol revenue, so this figure overlaps ProtocolRevenue rather than adding to Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid out to launch creators: the creator-nominated fee slots on creator-fee styles, LP fees on hookless styles, and buyback and burn on third-party launches.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Directional buy/sell fee skimmed inside the hook on hooked launch styles, set by the creator between 100 and 1000 bps (creatorFee + protocolFee from SwapFeesAccrued).
Fees.LP Fees: The pool's own Uniswap v4 LP fee on hookless launch styles, collected through LiquidityCustody (FeesCollected plus the matching ProtocolFeePaid).

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: The 30 bps protocol share of trade volume, routed to FeeRouter.
Revenue.Token Buy Back: ETH spent buying back HKRS, the protocol's own token, and burning it.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: The 30 bps protocol share of trade volume, routed to FeeRouter.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: HKRS bought back and burned, valued in ETH: the automatic buyback hook on the HKRS pool, plus the discretionary buybacks the team runs out of the protocol's fee share.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: Hook fees paid to the creator-nominated fee slots on creator-fee launch styles.
SupplySideRevenue.LP Fees: Uniswap v4 LP fees paid to the creator on hookless launch styles.
SupplySideRevenue.Buy Back On Third-Party Launches: Fees spent buying back and burning a third-party launch's own token, which accrues to that token's holders rather than to the protocol's.

protos.description: SettleTON is the First TON Liquidity Pool Index Fund that maximises yields by helping users invest in the most reliable TON Projects in just one click.
protos.methodology:
The methodology for calculating the total TVL is based on analyzing liquidity pool data and LP token balances. 
For each Vaults we iterate through all LP tokens and calculate their price based on following onchain data: (reserve0, reserve1, total_lp_supply)
For each pool, a calculation is performed to determine the equivalent amount of TON based on the current pool reserves and the share of LP tokens held. 
This calculation takes into account the reserve ratios and adjusts the token value to TON.
For multi-indices, the TVL of all pools is summed up, while for single indices, the value of the sole pool is used. The final TVL is represented in TON, and the index price is calculated by dividing the TVL by the total supply of the index.

protos.name: Kerne
protos.description: Kerne is a synthetic dollar protocol on Base. kUSD is minted and redeemed one to one against USDC through an on chain peg stability module, and every circulating kUSD is backed by USDC reserves held in the PSM contracts. Backing is published hourly as a signed proof of reserves that anyone can recompute from public RPC reads. kUSD itself pays no yield. skUSD, the staked form of kUSD, is the protocol's yield bearing receipt, designed to earn a delta neutral basis yield. Reported TVL is the USDC held in the PSM reserves that back circulating kUSD one to one.
protos.methodology: TVL is the USDC reserve held by Kerne's Peg Stability Module (PSM) contracts on Base, which back all circulating kUSD 1:1. kUSD is minted 1:1 from USDC through the live mint PSM (0xaBDE1138) and redeemed 1:1 back to USDC through the redeem PSM (0xFf3025ec); a prior mint PSM (0x07eBb486) still retains USDC from earlier mints. All PSM USDC reserves are summed; the kUSD supply itself is not added (that would double count). This matches the published headline TVL at kerne.fi/api/stats. The v1 KerneVault is intentionally excluded: it has been superseded by a v2 redeploy, its deposits are disabled, and its totalAssets() reports off-chain balances that are not part of the on-chain PSM reserves.

protos.name: popi
protos.description: Gacha bonding-curve memecoin launchpad; raises are escrowed on the curve until graduation, then migrated to the chain's DEX (PumpSwap on Solana, Uniswap v3 on Robinhood Chain).
protos.methodology: popi is a bonding-curve memecoin launchpad on two chains. TVL is the quote asset escrowed in live (still-bonding, not-yet-graduated) launches. Robinhood Chain: we count the native ETH held by the shared UUPS launchpad proxy, which equals the sum of every bonding launch's escrow excluding graduated funds (migrated to Uniswap). Solana: each launch owns a System-owned vault PDA (seeds ["vault", launchPubkey]); we enumerate Launch accounts, exclude Graduated ones (migrated to PumpSwap), and sum the native SOL in the surviving vaults. Launched tokens themselves and post-graduation DEX liquidity are not counted here.

The 1st perspective, "RWA" valuation, represents the total value of the tokenized forward carbon credits, and is computed as the present value of the on-chain forward credits (ERC1155), based on their exchange rate to CRISP tokens (ERC20) and subsequent USDC value, summed-up.The 2nd perspective, "pool2", represents the total value locked up in our staking contract, and it's calculated by adding up the value of all the LP tokens that are staked. The LP tokens represent the amount of liquidity that has been provided to the Solid World platform.
